visual.method: The letter V (upper-case roman, from this table) in the cycle's punch outline, a rectangle-rounded (Small upright rectangle with rounded corners around a roman letter, lower case to about O, capitals after), per Sir Charles J. Jackson, English Goldsmiths and Their Marks (1921), facsimiles; Bradbury's Book of Hallmarks. The letterform is a matching typeface, not the office's own punch.
visual.credit: Drawn by Heirloom from the published descriptions; not a photograph.

entries.name: Britannia
entries.looks_like: A seated female figure with a shield and spear.
entries.means: From 27 Mar 1697 the Britannia standard (95.8% silver) was compulsory. Its marks are the figure of Britannia and a lion's head erased, in place of the lion passant and leopard's head. Sterling was allowed again from 1 Jun 1720, and Britannia stayed optional afterwards. From 1697 to 1701 only London could assay; Chester used Britannia marks 1701-1719/20.

visual.holder: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
visual.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Open Access (CC0); cut out and toned by Heirloom.
